articleTitle: Shielding the upper deck of a ship by the use of a wide mashed wire grid
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.

articleTitle: Principles of shipboard grounding
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.

articleTitle: Introduction to shipboard EMI
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.

articleTitle: HF-Shielding of cots components in naval shipbuilding
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.

articleTitle: In-SITU EMI testing of large naval radar systems using a vibrating intrinsic reverberation chamber (VIRC)
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.

articleTitle: Shielding effectiveness of concrete buildings
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The prediction of the shielding effectiveness of concrete structures is a fundamental aspect of the architectural design phase of purpose built control centres. These buildings designed with a functional requirement to house sensitive control equipment; malfunction of such equipment may lead to loss of life and impact on revenue service. In this paper, a simple analytical approach is proposed to influence the design of buildings such that the structure provides adequate attenuation to hostile electromagnetic ambient and potential electromagnetic pulses. Comparison with numerical methods is provided. The effect of moisture content on the shielding effectiveness of a concrete wall is outlined.

articleTitle: Analysis of the electromagnetic radiation behaviour of motherboard-subboard structures
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Due to its antenna nature, subboard-on-motherboard structures act as unintentional radiators of electromagnetic fields. The magnitude of the electromagnetic emissions can exceed even the CISPR 22 limits, when high-speed signals are routed through the interboard connector. A worst-case analysis of the maximum field strength radiated from two mutually-parallel motherboard-subboard PCBs is presented in this paper. A detailed investigation of the radiation behaviour of motherboard-subboard structures leads to the conclusion that with a suitable pin configuration of the interboard connector the field emission can be considerably reduced. It is shown that further field suppression can be achieved, if grounding posts are introduced into the system design.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband planar monopole antenna for operation in the 3-20 GHz band
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: An ultra-wideband rectangular planar monopole antenna with an operation bandwidth larger than 20 GHz is designed using the bevelling technique. In this work it will be proved that instead of a square planar monopole, a rectangular planar monopole with double bevel is a better way to increase the antenna bandwidth at least 10:1, without degrading the stability of the radiation pattern. Also the ground plane size influence onto impedance and radiation pattern was investigated. Simulated and experimental results have close convergence.

articleTitle: Application of FEKO program to the analysis of SAR on human head modeling at 900 and 1800 MHz from a handset antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, a human head with a monopole handset antenna is simulated by using FEKO program for the analysis of specific absorption rates (SAR) in the human head at 900 and 1800 MHz. The human head model is homogeneous and simulated with the brain equivalent material. The applied antenna is consisted of a quarter-wavelength monopole mounted on a mobile handset (treated as a metal box), operated at 900 and 1800 MHz frequencies and radiated power of 0.32 Watt. The purpose of this simulation is for calculation of 1 g average SAR on the above systems, which is recommended its limit value 1.6 W/kg in FCC and ICNIRP. In addition to this result, 10 g average SAR is calculated, and the comparison between the results of 900 MHz and that of 1800 MHz is done.

articleTitle: The lower characteristic ELF altitude of the Earth-ionosphere waveguide: Schumann resonance observations and aeronomical estimates
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Propagation of ELF fields in the Earth-ionosphere waveguide is treated in terms of a two-dimensional method with two complex characteristic altitudes as actual propagation parameters. The day-to-night variations of the lower characteristic altitude are estimated in two different ways: theoretically, on the basis of the parameter's physical model and representative day- and night-time conductivity profiles for the lower ionospheric D-region, and experimentally, from systematic observations of the background electromagnetic signal in the Schumann resonance (SR) frequency range. A simple technique for considerably eliminating undetectable factors (the average current moment, the ionospheric properties over sources, etc.) and smoothing resonance effects in experimental data is applied. It is found that theoretical-aeronomical and experimental estimates are in a reasonable agreement, showing an approx. 20 to 25% day-to-night increase in the lower characteristic altitude within the lower SR frequency range (SR I to III).

articleTitle: Comparison of radiated emissions from different heatsink configurations
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: This paper investigates by means of numerical simulations the influence that different heatsink configurations have on the generation of radiated emissions. The effects of a subdivision of the heatsink among the different switching devices of a switched-mode power supply are examined. The plots of the electric near field for different excitation conditions are analyzed in terms of the surface current density distribution on the heatsink configurations. The electric far field as a function of frequency is obtained transforming the time-domain waveforms into the frequency domain and the influence of the heatsink geometry and source location is discussed.

articleTitle: On the relationship of information theory and electromagnetism
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Limitations imposed by the laws of electromagnetism on achievable MIMO channel capacity are studied in its general form. The approach is a two-fold one. First, the channel correlation argument is used to demonstrate that the minimum antenna spacing under any scattering conditions is at least half a wavelength. Secondly, using a plane-wave spectrum expansion of a generic electromagnetic wave combined with the Nyquist sampling theorem in the spatial domain, we show that the laws of electromagnetism limit the minimum antenna spacing to half a wavelength, /spl lambda//2, (in the case of 1-D antenna apertures) only asymptotically, when the number of antennas n/spl rarr//spl infin/. For a finite number of antennas, this limit is slightly less than /spl lambda//2. In any case, the number of antennas and, consequently, the MIMO capacity is limited for a given aperture size. This is a scenario-independent limit.

articleTitle: Modeling of common mode interferences produced by a switched mode power supply
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: This work deals with the examination of the influence of interconnections on fast transients in power electronic circuits and the creation of a simulation tool for modeling power systems with taking into account this phenomenon. The simulation tool must provide exact models of semiconductors and the possibility to implement parasitic influences of conductors. The PEEC method allows to represent the interconnection structure as an equivalent passive circuit. This fact enables the analysis of the power electronic circuit under consideration of interconnections. Ansoft Simplorer/spl reg/ is a wide spread professional code for modeling of power circuits. It can be expanded by additional elements programmed in C++. In this work a PEEC model is implemented into Simplorer/spl reg/. Thus, it's possible to simulate the interconnections simultaneously with the standard lumped circuits.

articleTitle: EMI measurements for aging control and fault diagnosis in active devices
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: This work presents and discusses the results of a measurement campaign aimed at demonstrating the effects of aging and faults on the spectrum produced by an electronic device. The evaluations evidence a high spectrum sensibility to the mentioned events, and suggest a methodology for apparatus monitoring, which is particularly useful in connection with critical devices, in order to decide whether to activate their stand-by units and/or to decide whether to replace or to service them. The results obtained support the theoretic feasibility of the method, whereas the practical one requires further investigations.

articleTitle: Structure and EMC simulation of vehicle radiocommunication base station
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The paper presents structure and complex EMC approach to design and electromagnetic modeling of multifunctional mobile radio transmit base station of the automatic communication and control system. Several modes of the base station and results of design and computer simulation of the station are described. Two models (MoM and FDTD) are considered for analysis of the vehicle antenna array. Broadband matching networks are synthesized for the antenna array. A simulation of far and near electromagnetic fields of the broadband matched antenna station is worked out.

articleTitle: Progress in the PLC development during the years 2003-2004
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: This report presents the progress achieved in the development and implementation of the PLC technology during the years 2003 and 2004. It presents the progress on the standardization work for products and for network standards. It also gives a general view about the deployment of PLC networks in Europe, in USA and also in some other parts of the world.

articleTitle: Inclusion of an automatic adaptive sampling method in NEC
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: As sampling is taking place, the most active regions of the spectrum can be identified (i.e. the vicinity of spectral peaks). By selectively increasing the spectral density within those regions improves the quality of the total spectral representation reducing at the same time the global number of samples, and therefore, the total calculation time. The Blumer index is useful for adapting the sampling density of a calculated or measured spectrum.

articleTitle: Discrete nonlinear EMC analysis: principles, capabilities and application restrictions
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Principles, advantages, limitations and hardware requirements for implementation of the discrete nonlinear EMC system analysis (DNA-EMC) are described. DNA EMC implies application of discrete models of the electromagnetic environment and of accumulative signal in radio receivers, high order polynomial models of nonlinear transfer characteristics, polychotomous identification procedures for interference sources; Hilbert transform to extract signal envelope when modeling the amplitude-phase conversion and detection processes and digital signal processing to analyze signal distortion during its reception in severe electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: De-embedding microwave fixtures with the genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Direct measurement of frequency characteristics of a device under test (DUT) at microwave frequencies is often difficult due to some intervening fixture used for feeding the DUT. In contrast to a great number of self-calibration techniques, the method proposed in the paper does not require any calibration standard and allows us to de-embed an effect of the fixture from experimental data obtained at the network analyzer reference plane being based only on characteristics of the "Thru" experiment. It is shown that the traditional de-embedding problem being posed in a finite frequency range may be reduced to a problem of fitting the characteristics of the "Thru" experiment. The latter is proposed to be solved by using the genetic algorithm. A special trick is suggested to take fixture power loss into consideration, which sometimes is necessary to increase the goodness of fitting the characteristics. The results of the experiments performed have validated a high efficiency of the method proposed.

articleTitle: Advanced software for planning and optimization of spectrum monitoring networks
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Short description of new software for planning and optimization of spectrum monitoring networks or groups of monitoring stations is presented. The software permits to calculate service areas provided by various monitoring functions, such as listening, emission parameters measurement and direction finding, as well as location accuracy templates under triangulation location operations, those are distributions of the location accuracy throughout an overall location service area.

articleTitle: Time-domain and frequency characteristics of ultrawideband signals for radiocommunication systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The time and frequency analysis of ultrawideband (UWB) signals for radiocommunication systems is presented in the paper. The results of computation are shown. A process of synthesis of the ultrawideband signals from the spectrum for different parameters is analyzed. Transmission of UWB signals through an ideal radio channel using single Gaussian pulse as an example was presented. Time and frequency analysis of ultrawideband signals is useful for EMC issues.

articleTitle: Program kit to study human head exposed to EM radiation
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Personal wireless communication device are used in immediate vicinity of the body, producing high localized RP energy deposition. The motivation of this research is to investigate possible influence of the EM devices on the live organisms, which may result of local tissues overheating. The proprietary computer program package based on the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method for electromagnetic (EM) and thermal analysis of inhomogeneous, as well as method of auxiliary sources (MAS) for partially homogeneous problems was developed. Temperature rise in heterogeneous realistic head model (downscaled to child head size) exposed to mobile phone radiation at 835 MHz is studied. 12 pt. SAR and power absorption in different materials is investigated.

articleTitle: Effect of the design of electric-power transmission lines on their electromagnetic compatibility with biosphere
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: In designing of overhead and cable lines (OH and CLs), and their laying and operation, it is necessary to take into account the influence of electrostatic and electromagnetic fields generated by the charges on, and the currents in, cable conductors, on biosphere and environment. Special attention is to be paid to the level of electromagnetic field in the immediate vicinity of OH and CLs, since this field acts on biosphere representatives on the cell level and may cause degeneration of living cells and results in subsequent serious diseases. An analytical and a numerical procedure reported here enable prediction of the electromagnetic situation along the routes of OH and CLs and formulation of measures making it possible to reduce the electromagnetic-field intensity around them.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic environment in aircraft by wireless LAN system and its possibility of interference on avionics
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: This paper describes electromagnetic field distribution and strength in a Boeing 747-400 cabin by IEEE 802.11a/b/g LAN (WLAN). Emission from WLAN access point and terminal is measured first. Then, WLAN signal distribution is estimated by WLAN throughput distribution in the aircraft. WLAN signal level has been measured in several observation points when multiple access points and terminals are used simultaneously. The signal level is compared with the emission and susceptibility recommendations in RTCA DO-160D. Immunity of 32 avionic systems is examined in WLAN frequencies. The results show that the signal variation in the cabin becomes more than 10 dB. The signal level by multiple WLAN access points and terminals has been 15-30 dB higher than recommended emission limits of RTCA DO-160D Category M. And the peak level is as high as the susceptibility test level of DO-160D Category T. The immunity test has shown that no avionic systems under test demonstrate anomalies.

articleTitle: On the electromagnetic field excitation of smoothly curved wires
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: A smoothly curved wire of arbitrary geometric form excited by an external electromagnetic field is considered. It has been shown that the exact mixed-potential integral equations (MPIE's) for the induced current and scalar potential along the wire can approximately be reduced to a system of telegrapher equations for each Fourier mode. Corresponding frequency dependent transmission line per-unit length parameters, inductive and capacitive, now slowly depend on the length of the curve. As example the coupling of a plane wave to a vertical semi-elliptical loop above a perfectly conducting ground is considered. The result of the calculation is in a good agreement with NEC.

articleTitle: Synthesis of nonlinear compensators on basis of operational equations for electronic devices protected from low-frequency noises
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: A method of nonlinear compensation of low-frequency noises in complex electronic devices is considered at two-tone high-frequency excitation of an external electromagnetic field. The method supposes construction of a nonlinear operational equation of a compensator and its use for synthesis of a nonlinear compensating circuit. The operational equation is designed on basis of multidimensional transfer functions of electronic device obtained by Picard's iterations. The example of synthesis of the nonlinear compensating circuit is considered, quality of compensation is estimated and comparison of the method with known analogue is carried out.

articleTitle: Structure and radiation of broadband ionosphere research station (HAARP)
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The paper presents structure, main characteristics and radiation modeling of broadband ionosphere station stands for High Frequency Active Auroral Research Program (HAARP). The fundamental goal of this investigation is to explore and understand natural phenomena occurring in the Earth's ionosphere and near-space environment. Information derived from this research will have major value in the design of future communication and navigation systems. Structure of the antenna array, transmitter units and radiation computer modeling of the station are described in the paper.

articleTitle: Multifractal analysis for the ULF geomagnetic data during the Guam earthquake
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: In our previous papers we have shown that the fractal (monofractal) dimension (D/sub 0/) showed a significant increase before the Guam earthquake occurred on August 8, 1993. In order to have a further support to this precursory effect, we have carried out the corresponding multifractal analysis (by means of detrended fluctuation analysis) for the same data to study the statistical self-similar properties in a wide range of scales. We have analyzed the ULF geomagnetic data (the must intense H component) observed at Guam observatory. As the result, we have found that we could observe significant changes in the multifractal parameters at Guam such that /spl alpha//sub min/ showed a meaningful decrease about 25 days before the earthquake and correspondingly /spl Delta//spl alpha/ increased because /spl alpha//sub max/ exhibited no significant change at all. Correspondingly, the generalized multifractal dimension Dq(>1) showed a significant decrease (whereas Dq(q<0) showed no change) and D/sub 0/(=Dq(q=0) (as already found in our previous papers) is reconfirmed to increase before the earthquake. These multifractal characteristics seem to be a further support that these changes are closely associated with the earthquake as a precursor to the Guam earthquake.

articleTitle: A weakly directional antenna with the controlled ellipticity coefficient
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: A weakly directional antenna, which configuration allows to control the position of the unitary ellipticity coefficient throughout the visible angles domain is proposed. The analysis of an opportunity for such antennas to be used in the antenna arrays having the controlled polarized characteristics is performed.

articleTitle: Planning the aircraft cable assembly lines, taking into account intersystem electromagnetic compatibility
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The article considers the potential of using the graphs and the algorithms of their optimization for planning the aircraft and space vehicle cable networks, considering the requirements of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). Tracing of the cable assemblies, taking into account the intersystem EMC, has been discussed as an example.

articleTitle: Airborne electronic equipment immunity to the very low frequency electromagnetic field influence (civil aviation standards problems)
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Airborne electronic equipment reliable operation is critical in ensuring flight safety. The civil aviation RTCA/DO-160E and EUROCAE/ED-14E standard procedures and environmental test criteria for testing airborne equipment aimed on the aircraft onboard electromagnetic emission sources. Taking in an account the possibility of external very low frequency electromagnetic field influence on the electronic onboard equipment it is possible to find a number of severe problems. Analyses of unspecified frequency bands and requirements for the testing aircraft electronic onboard equipment were conducted in this paper.

articleTitle: Error rates for MSK signals in Nakagami-fading channels for the local alarm radiotechnical systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: MSK signals are widely used for information transferring in the local alarm radiotechnical systems. Noise-immunity of the coherent reception of the MSK signals in the presence of Nakagami fading is considered in this paper.

articleTitle: Influence of frequency, direction finder parameters and actual terrain topography on features of Kogan-Pavliouk location templates
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Influences of frequency, direction finder parameters and actual terrain topography on features of location accuracy templates, also known as Kogan-Pavliouk location templates, are considered. The template shows a distribution of accuracy of source of emission location, obtained by a triangulation operation using at least two separated DF-s, throughout an overall location service area. This location service area is a part of common FD service area of a group of DF stations. It is demonstrated that location is the most limited function in comparison with other monitoring functions such as listening, emission parameters measurements and direction finding because at least two individual direction finders should be involved to provide location by triangulation operation. This function is also the most influenced by various instrumental and operational factors as well as by actual terrain topography. These features are illustrated by results of exact calculations.

articleTitle: EMC analysis of double-band antenna of ionospheric station HAARP
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The paper presents structure, some characteristics and EMC analysis of broadband double-band antenna for an ionospheric station stands HAARP. This antenna is main base element of large antenna array of the station. Power excitation, current distribution, broadband matching problem for the double-band antenna are considered in the work. Structure of the antenna and computer EMC modeling of near electromagnetic field of the base element are described in the paper.

articleTitle: An approach to inductance modelling for power PCB interconnections: FDTD model-based extraction
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The significance of parasitic impedances of the connecting structures in power electronic converters (PCB interconnects) increases with frequency and switching speed and influences transients and radiated EMI. Design aspects such as physical layout and interconnect routing requires accurate extraction of parasitic parameters. This paper presents a computational procedure for partly achieving this for typical power converter systems.

articleTitle: Computer-aided design of automatic antenna matching devices
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a problem of computer-aided design of an automatic matching devices controlled in wide frequency band. Method of matching of the complex impedance with a dynamic change in the given frequency band is proposed. A binary control algorithm of the automatic matching of the arbitrary complex loads is presented. A structure of ideal network and quantum and coding of variable network element values are described. Models of the real elements, macroelements and the whole matching device with taken into account of loss and parasitic parameters are presented. Results of computer-aided design and simulation of device characteristics in the given frequency band are represented.

articleTitle: Voltage fluctuation calculations in common and special cases
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: In the report the method of calculation of a flicker doze value is considered. Flicker doze characterizes intensity of voltage oscillations in power networks. This method is based on the use of standard flickermeter transfer function and obtained parameters of voltage fluctuation correlation functions. The results of calculations allow to compare expected values of voltage fluctuations in power networks to requests of the standards. In some cases in power networks it is possible to allow voltage fluctuation values, which exceed requests of the standards. The calculation of voltage fluctuation values in these cases is expedient for realizing in parallel with calculations of results of their negative effect degrees on a electric power equipment because of same correlation functions of voltage fluctuations in power supply networks.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of influence of a.c. traction current on the rail circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The experimental investigation of spectral structure of return traction current was done on the section with a.c. traction. The 25 and 75 Hz harmonics determined among the rest coincide with the signal current in rails. The information about spectral structure of traction current can be used at the design of new systems, which are applied in the railway, and in other spheres.

articleTitle: Stable time domain solution of EFIE via full-wave PEEC modeling
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The PEEC method is a wide-spread numerical method for creating full-wave models of interconnection structures in frequency and time domain being in use for modeling in EMC problems. The possible instabilities of time domain solutions, so-called late time instabilities, can complicate the use of the method. This paper studies the reason for instabilities and provides a method for stability improvement.

articleTitle: Planning a frigate ACC. to German VG-standards-some thoughts about integrating COTS- and MIL-STD-equipment
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Complex systems, containing power electronics, electric and electronic equipment for automation and control purposes, as well as devices for the external and also the internal communication need an EMC-planning in parallel to all development phases of the system. Watching the process from the first idea up to the hand-over to the final user the following development steps can be detected. It starts with the concept phase, followed by the definition and the construction phase and ends with the building phase. Especially in military projects only an EMC-planning according to a defined procedure assures a reliable system during its lifetime. The procedures used for military projects proofed also to be very useful in constructing and erecting civilian projects, like power or manufacturing plants, control and communication stations; as well as for mobile systems, like cars, ships and airplanes. Very sophisticated procedures are fixed in the German VG-standards (VG -VerteidigungsGerSt). But in no case the ideal way defined in these standards can be followed. One of the restrictions is given by the fact, that equipment must be integrated, which is not qualified ACC. to the VG-standards, for instance in many cases COTS-equipment (COTS = commercial of the shelf) or devices already tested ACC. to MIL-STD- or other military standards like STANAG must be used. The paper describes the structure of the EMC-program plan with its responsibilities, its technical content and the intrasystem measures to be taken. A special topic will be the comparison of limit values for radiated emissions (electric field versus magnetic field) and the distance conversion for radiated signals.

articleTitle: Calculation of electrical cable parameters for pulse propagation model
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: It is necessary to take into consideration nanosecond pulse propagation in bursts immunity tests arid in EMC research work. Electrical cable between pulse noise source and equipment influences on malfunction level. The model of pulse propagation in time domain is used for calculation. Parameters of power cables for the model and effects of propagation are discussed.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic field background in the urban area of Rome (Italy): the situation until 2001
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: It is presented the work performed by ISPESL, related to the analysis of the wide band electromagnetic field measurements, carried out in the urban area of Rome, in the period from 1998 to 2001. ISPESL carried out approximately 500 wide band measurements near the sites selected and proposed by the network companies for the installation of new radio base stations (SRB). The measurements have been carried out using a wide band probe equipped with an isotropic electric field probe, in areas where people stay for more than four hours. The results of the electromagnetic measurements have been compared with the electric field levels fixed by the Italian law to prevent hazardous due to long term people exposure to the electromagnetic field sources with frequency between 100 kHz-300 GHz, which is 6 V/m. The electric field levels have been shared in classes, to analyse the statistical distribution of the electric field levels measured and calculated in the urban environment of Rome.

articleTitle: Convolution techniques used for the prediction of induced current
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Transfer functions are used internationally for the assessment of air platforms that are required to fly through high intensity radiated field (HIRF) environments. These environments are expressed in the frequency domain in international standards. The same transfer functions can be used to predict the response of cable bundles to incident time domain environments. The time domain process is more mathematically complex than the simple extrapolation techniques used with HIRF environments and requires the construction of phase information before the prediction can be completed. This process is discussed in this paper along with suggestions for improvements of the currently used technique. These improvements include binding the prediction between a worst-case and best-case induced current as a result of the incident time domain environment.

articleTitle: Calculation of electromagnetic field characteristics in TEM-cell
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: In this paper the method of partial regions was used for obtaining the analytical expressions of electromagnetic field components in regular part of TEM-cell. An ability of highest waves types distribution in regular part of TEM-cell is shown, dispersion characteristics of highest waves types are found. The procedure of calculation of proper wave components in TEM-cell is considered and field structures are computed.

articleTitle: Model of diurnal/seasonal variations of ELF natural radio signal based on OTD data
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Knowledge of expected parameters of natural extremely low frequency (ELF) radio signal arriving from the global lightning activity to observatory is necessary when one looks for the signals originating from other sources, in particular, for the electromagnetic precursors of a future earthquake shock. The radio waves of seismic and cosmic origin might be expected in the bands of ultra-low (ULF, 0.01-3 Hz) and ELF (3 Hz-3 kHz), i.e., at frequencies where natural electromagnetic radiation exists in the Earth-ionosphere cavity. Radiation from the magnetosphere or from underground electric activity provides additional signals to be discriminated from the ordinary lightning induced pattern. We construct the model variations of natural ELF radio signal on the daily and monthly scales. The maps of global distribution of lightning flashes are used as initial data. These were recorded by the OTD satellite (optical transient detector) and by LIS (lightning image sensor). The model developed provides expected variations of the ELF power on the diurnal and seasonal scales thus describing typical behavior of Schumann resonance background.

articleTitle: The theoretical and experimental researches of electromagnetic influence from a traction electrosupply system on a railway circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The theoretical and experimental researches of electromagnetic influence on a railway lines from a traction electrosupply system were carried out. The mathematical model and computer program on its basis for evaluation of influence of traction current on railway circuits was proposed. Developed method was used for testing of an AC electric locomotive with asynchronous engines on electromagnetic compatibility with rail circuits. In some locomotive operation regimes the harmonious interference in railway circuits with frequencies that coincide with frequencies of signal currents used for interlocking and automatic locomotive signalization were registered.

articleTitle: The regional system of monitoring power quality parameters in real time
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The territorial system /spl Lt/PRORYV/spl Gt/ for technical control of electrical power quality parameters in real-time mode is described in this article. Some of the specified digital measuring devices together with measuring power quality are able to monitor the general parameters of electric power with the purpose of defining individual consumers' affect on power quality in the common connection point for several consumers according to RD 153-34.0-15.501-2002.

articleTitle: Diagnostic of environment with the help of low frequency noise radio interference by satellite data
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Low frequency emission in range of 100 Hz-20 kHz it is accepted to consider as radio interference, actually they are the useful tool for diagnostic and analysis of dynamic processes in environment. The usefulness of noise obtained on the "Intercosmos" satellite data is routine.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of radio links for radiocommunication systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The paper presents method of a design and analysis of digital radio links of small and medium capacity. Proper project of radio links is major problem for EMC issues. The most important aspects of radio waves propagation that must be taken into account by designer are discussed. The problem of antenna placing and heights are discussed in particular. Propagation loss and multipath attenuation are taken into consideration as another important EMC factors.

articleTitle: Validation, verification and calibration in numerical electromagnetics: canonical tests and comparisons
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Modeling and numerical simulation in electromagnetics is discussed in this paper with emphasize placed on validation, verification and calibration. Canonical examples from antennas, propagation to microstrip circuits are presented. Tests against measurements, when available, are also presented.

articleTitle: Low frequency common mode voltages in electrical cable runs
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Low frequency common mode voltages can produce malfunction of control and measuring systems. The sources of common mode voltages are electrical and magnetic fields of electrical equipment, electromagnetic coupling in electrical cable runs. Induced common mode voltage with 50 Hz frequency can be up to 100 V for electrical coupling, but less than 0.1 V for magnetic coupling.

articleTitle: Revision of the EMC directive
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The revision of the EMC Directive arose as a result of the EU Commission's program called SLIM (Simpler Legislation for the Internal Market) and of the Commission's efforts to improve legal security through a clearer and more precise text giving an answer to divergent interpretations of the actual EMC Directive 89/336/EEC. This paper will deal with the major changes brought by the planned new directive.

articleTitle: The methods of the reduction of coupling between antennas on aerospace vehicle
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Some new ways of the reduction of coupling between on-board antennas are considered. It is proposed to use for these objective optimized on geometric and electrophysical parameters a magnetodielectric covering, pin structure and spiral monolayer. It is analyzed physical mechanisms, which is underlying of attenuation characteristics of specified structures.

articleTitle: Fractal characteristics of the natural ULF emissions in relation to geomagnetic activity
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Fractal analysis of the ULF emissions registered at low-latitude observatory Guam (/spl Phi//sub m/=9/spl deg/N, /spl Lambda//sub m/=225/spl deg/) has been performed. Dynamics of scaling characteristics (spectral exponents /spl beta/ and fractal dimensions D0) has been analyzed depending on the level of geomagnetic activity and in relation to the nearby earthquake of August 8, 1993. It is found that the spectrum of ULF emissions exhibits power law behavior S(f)/spl infin/f-/spl beta/ which is typical for fractal (self-affine) time series. It is also revealed that spectral exponent /spl beta/ varies in the range /spl beta/=0.7-2.5 in correlation with Kp-index of geomagnetic activity, and manifests a downward tendency when approaching the earthquake date. The results obtained are discussed on the basis of the SOC (self-organized criticality) approach to study the ULF emission source dynamics.

articleTitle: Algorithm for interference suppression in the biorthogonal antenna system with the signal circular polarization
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: A processing algorithm for signals received by the biorthogonal antenna system, providing the suppression of the linear polarization interference in the radio channel with the signal circular polarization given the a priori unknown orientation of the field vector generated by the interference source is suggested. The given algorithm guarantees the efficient interference suppression even with the signal-interference ratio being equal to less than unity.

articleTitle: Application of the MAS to cavities with apertures in problems of EME
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: This article considers EM ecology (EME) problems on cavities with apertures. Method of auxiliary sources (MAS) is used as a method of investigation. Frequency range of research is resonant for object. Diffraction of electromagnetic plan wave on the semiclosed, perfectly conducted surface with some apertures is considered. Investigation is realized by numerical experiment.

articleTitle: A study of the dissipation characteristics of antennas placed on the revolution bodies of the resonant sizes
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: A research and methodical apparatus, allowing to estimate the dissipative properties of the constructions, where the low element antenna arrays for different radio facilities are placed on, has been developed. Numerical studies for the construction in the form of a rotation body of the resonant sizes have been conducted.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic fields of mobile radio communication and danger estimation for the population
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The EMF danger of mobile radio communication for the population is estimated. The influence of EMF of cellular telephones on users' brain (adults and children) is considered. Electromagnetic conditions around base stations and possible influence on the population health are presented.

articleTitle: On simulating light radiation from surface and underwater sources of gamma-rays
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The paper is devoted to theoretical research of processes of generation and distribution of light radiation from surface and subsurface underwater high-energy non-stationary sources of gamma-rays. The special attention is given to influence of an interface of two media with different physical properties on parameters of the light signal registered by the removed receiver of light radiation. These researches have the important practical significance for development of optical means of remote monitoring of high-energy processes of a natural and artificial origin.

articleTitle: Different linearizing techniques to improve electromagnetic compatibility in SiGe LNA
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: In this work three different structures are proposed to improve the linearity of SiGe amplifiers. The first structure, AFCE has the possibility of obtaining high linearity and wide bandwidth with low-level noise figure, without degrading the power gain. The second configuration called CERCC in a very high linearization is obtained but in a narrower band than the Active feedback configuration. The third structure is an alternative of the previous, but using only one resonant circuit in the collector and an inductor in the emitter.

articleTitle: Mutual inductance between wires in helically twisted power cables
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The arrangement of the conductors in a multi-core power cable leads to a situation where various conductor loops are built up. One or several loops are formed by the phase and neutral conductors with the operational current flowing in these conductors. A further loop is built up by the protective earth conductor which is connected to the equipotential bonding system at several locations. The area of this loop is essentially arranged outside of the power cable. The inductive coupling from the phase conductor loops into that loop causes common mode voltages in the protective earth system with consequent common mode currents. It can be demonstrated that this effect even takes place in the case of balanced phase currents in the cable. Numerical simulations and parameter studies were carried out in order to describe this effect quantitatively and to investigate the influence of different cable parameters onto the resulting common mode voltages.

articleTitle: Low-energy laser radiation bioefficiency in model object and some actual problems of radiobiology of nonionizing radiations
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: While infra-red low-energy impulse laser bioefficiency has been researched in Drosophila melanogaster one and two maximums of laser stimulation on the curves "dose-effect" have been revealed . In the second part some problems of radiobiology are discussed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of shielding effectiveness on system level by electromagnetic topology based modeling
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The confidence in shielding effectiveness (SE) measurements on enclosures according to IEC TS 61587-3 is evaluated. A methodical analysis using an electromagnetic topology (EMT) based model is carried out to find the electromagnetic (EM) critical aspects. The EMT model represents the interaction between base and auxiliary components which are necessary for testing. As shown in examples, each local coupling effect can be investigated by means of an appropriate, numerical or experimental method. It is displayed how the EMT facilitates the translation of local estimations into the global SE test result.

articleTitle: Recent developments in lightening test standards for aircraft and avionics
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: There is a general movement towards synchronisation of the many diverse standards applicable to avionics and aircraft testing in both the civilian and military fields. Foremost of these and widely accepted as an 'international' standard is the new edition of RTCA/DO160D. The latest additions are embodied in change No. 3 from December 2002. This paper provides an overview of the new standard focusing on the lightening test part and differentiates between special requirements, outlining the impact on test equipment and test load and the authors experience in carrying out these tests.

articleTitle: Reduction of /spl Lt/back-door/spl Gt/ radiative coupling, review and analysis of classical methods and study of an innovative technique
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Techniques of back-door radiative coupling limitation are reviewed, including microwave gaskets and special assembling methods. These techniques help one to protect electronics against high frequency electromagnetic radiations like radar or high power microwave (HPM). An other way consisting of absorbing material placed into the equipment box is also examined. Measure of shielding effectiveness prove the efficiency of this technique, which has to be taken in account with statistical electromagnetic (STEM) tools.

articleTitle: Asymptotic optimality of random PSK signature ensembles
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Selection of a proper signature ensemble is the point of a special care in designing code division multiple access (DS CDMA) systems. When the receiver complexity beyond that of a single user algorithm is not affordable, Welch-bound ensembles minimizing intensity of the multiple access interference (MAI) are optimal. In this paper we show that for random signature sets the mean square deviation of MM power from the Welch bound drops in nearly inverse proportion with growth of K/N, where K is number of users and N is the spreading factor. Thereby, the fact of asymptotic (K/spl Gt/N) convergence in probability of random sets to the Welch-bound ones is demonstrated.

articleTitle: The changes of parameters of space plasma as a signal about a pollution of the environment
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The outcomes of simultaneous "Intercosmos" satellite measurements of magnetic and electrical component a of low frequency emissions field, low-energy electrons and density and temperature of ionospheric plasma are analyzed. The results of supervision are discussed in comparison with ionospheric anomalies simultaneously observed on board of Japan satellite ISS-b. It is established, that in Barents and Kara seas area observation results of simultaneous small-scale changes (fluctuations) of plasma parameters have coincided with zones of the increased contents of cesium (/sup 137/Cs) in bottom sediments. We proposed a method of detection of radiological contaminations (pollutions) based on results of complex analysis of satellite measurements of intensity a magnetic and electrical component of a low frequency emission field, and plasma parameters at satellite orbit heights.

articleTitle: Electrical decoupling device effectiveness for radiofrequency noise protection
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The electrical decoupling devices or signal conditioners are applied in the medical equipment, in control and measuring systems and in different electronic apparatus. Signal conditioners give separation of input and output signal circuits. EMC test method and result of tests are presented.

articleTitle: Estimation of possible meanings of electromagnetic compatibility of radio-electronic systems when using "supersolution" algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Analytic relations allowing to estimate the possible meanings of the signal/noise ratio depending on the parameters of antenna system and signals (number and step of radiator displacement, receiving signals covariance degree) are suggested. The relations are obtained for the contemporary methods of adaptive spatial filtration and estimation of spatial spectrum using the inverse covariance matrix. The results of mathematical modeling of signal processing based on the algorithm are given. Global character of radio-electronic systems use causes sufficient complication of electromagnetic situation. Efficient use of separated frequencies and ensuring desired accuracy of radio-electronic systems functioning under these circumstances is possible only when guaranteeing the set level of indirect radiation. In these terms the answer to the questions of ensuring the electromagnetic compatibility and electromagnetic ecology is connected to the increase of spatial selectivity when radiating and receiving radio signals. The approach realization basis is forming of required parameters of antenna pattern.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation strategies in wireless propagation and coverage planning
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents two-dimensional (2D) user-friendly, tailored with attractive and useful graphical user interfaces (GUI), Matlab propagation packages based on the classical knife-edge model and the parabolic equation method that can handle realistic propagation scenarios with non-flat, arbitrarily-designed and user-selected terrain profiles. Any 2D propagation scenario may be built by the user, and field vs. range and/or height profiles can be simulated.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of periodical frequency shift for radio frequency emission suppression in DC/DC converter
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: A DC/DC converter is the source of radio frequency noise. Emission reduction by switching frequency shifts is proposed. Frequency shifts up to 30% can give more than 20 dB noise reduction in theory. Frequency shifts 40-70% are less effective due to higher harmonics composition. Experiments show 10 dB noise reduction for 20% frequency shifts.

articleTitle: Utilization of radiation coupling effects to analyze subsurface structures of complex dielectric bodies
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The inverse scattering problem described in this paper is part of the quasi-tomographic comet nucleus sounding experiment CONSERT of the comet-mission Rosetta. This part of the experiment is based on the utilization of radiation coupling effects between the CONSERT antenna system on the Rosetta-Lander and the subsurface structure of the comet nucleus in the vicinity of the Lander. The scientific aim of this part of CONSERT is the reconstruction of the subsurface structure at the landing site, especially in view of the still open question: "Is a comet nucleus surround by a dust layer or not?". To solve this inverse scattering problem the line-of-sight link between Rosetta Orbiter and Lander will be used to measure the back lobes of the CONSERT Lander antenna with high angular resolution.

articleTitle: Suppression of interfering signals by means of the partially controlled monopulse antenna arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: In the report we present new analytical methods of the /spl Lt/partial/spl Gt/ null synthesis in sum and difference patterns of amplitude sum-difference monopulse antenna arrays (MAA) with simultaneous and separate beam forming, with the different ways of stabilizing the equal signal direction. Here we give their comparative analysis and the quasioptimal method of the MAA control as well.

articleTitle: Cost-effective mitigation measures concerning conducted emission of resistance welding inverters
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Resulting from the constantly increasing number of electrical and electronic appliances in both commercial and private spheres and the ongoing process of standardisation in the field of electromagnetic compatibility, there is a growing consciousness regarding possible electromagnetic interference problems of appliances. In the case of resistance welding equipment, special attention is paid to the occurring electromagnetic emissions because of the high rated-power parameters and the intermittent operation of these devices. Different noise mitigation measures, considering the special characteristics of the generation and propagation of disturbances in the case of resistance welding inverters are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Microwave radiation caused by double gamma-source
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The microwave radiation (MWR) of air plasma created by a double gamma source is considered. The second source arises near the first with some time lag. The estimation of the plasma aerial temperature is carried out at the moment of generation of a coherent pulse by the second source. For incoherent bremsstrahlung the radio brightness temperature time dependence is calculated for incoherent source of bremsstrahlung.

articleTitle: The combined influence of the static magnetic field and microwave radiation on conformation of nucleoid in living cells
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The physical reasons of conformation change of nucleoid in living cells under action of microwave radiation are investigated. The mechanism based on cooperative influence of a constant magnetic field and a high-frequency electric field on own fluctuations of nucleoid with a variable specific charge is offered. In conditions of resonances on frequency of an electric field and Larmor frequency of a magnetic field the maximum probabilities for the fixed values of angular coordinate of the center of mass of nucleoid is obtained. In this case values of a constant magnetic field are multiple to the relation of frequency of change of a specific charge to average value of a specific charge. Dependence of biological effect both on parameters of microwave radiation and on a static magnetic field is proved.

articleTitle: Nonlinear compensation in electronic systems at two-tone high-frequency excitation
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: An universal method of suppression of the intermodulation products in output signals of nonlinear electronic systems is considered at two-tone high-frequency excitation of an external electromagnetic field. The distorting system is represented as /spl Lt/a black or grey box/spl Gt/ and linearization of its characteristic is carried out with the help of isolation of the linear functional from Volterra polynomial describing an input-output relation of the initial electronic system. Compensation of nonlinear transformation of a detector is performed with use of the measured sets of input and output signals. Quality of executed compensation is estimated.

articleTitle: Power autotransformer electromagnetic radiation analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: This work describes power autotransformer radiation model. Experimental results have been compared with calculation. We suggest a method for diagnosing technical condition of power transformer according to its electromagnetic radiation.

articleTitle: NMR investigation of the same charged gelling biosystems for drug capsulation
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: It is proposed a series of new NMR relaxometry, diffusometry, spectroscopy techniques for the development of drug capsulation technology. On the basis of this NMR study a new capsulation system, the same charged gelling biosystem, was proposed. The nanostructure properties of the gelling bio-system including the phase diagram, nanopore and aggregate radii, drug release rate, system stability were measured using a new diffusion-specific probe, the same charged surfactant micelles, and theoretical approach of diffusion problem with complex variable representation. Drug release rate from the bio-capsule was determined using new NMR localization method without the application of the magnetic field gradients. The stability of the capsulating nanobiosystems was controlled by NMR relaxometry of water protons and parallely by the DSC and CD methods. The results show high sensitivity of the NMR methods to study homogeneous hydrogels with low volume fraction, an agreement with the X-ray diffraction data and promising perspectives for the use of the same charged gelling biosystems as high drug capacity, rate-controlled, bioadhesive media in pharmacology.

articleTitle: Determining the intermodulation intercept points by SPICE of weakly nonlinear circuits connected in cascade
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The intermodulation intercept points of weakly nonlinear circuits are studied. The output second and third order intercept points are obtained with SPICE intermodulation components. Cascade stages of nonlinear circuits are analyzed and the effect of poor matching in cascade stages is show, this affects the accuracy in the prediction of IP3 by conventional engineering formula.

articleTitle: Investigation of EMC in high-speed on-chip transmission lines by a new hybrid quasi-static finite difference-FEM technique
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: In this paper we present a new computational technique to investigate wave phenomena and EMC/EMI interactions in high speed transmission lines and interconnects on the chip level. The proposed time-domain method is based on the very different nature of the electromagnetic problem in the conductors and semiconductors, compared to the insulating media that separate conducting regions and fill the intermediate volume. Therefore, the purely static problem in the regions filled with silicon oxide is totally separated from the diffusion problem in the conducting regions. The latter one is solved by means of a simple and efficient DuFort-Frankel technique using finite differences, while the static problem is dealt with by means of a finite element method with coarse meshing, since outside the conductors the field variations are much less intense. In each time step, the problems in the two regions are appropriately coupled by means of proper interface conditions.

articleTitle: EMF measurement tasks and frequency selective evaluation methods for RF-communication facilities
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: In this paper we point out the most relevant content of the ICNIRP guidelines and derive from these standard EMF measurement tasks such as 'In Situ Measurements', 'Compliance Assessment Measurements' and 'RF-Monitoring'. Different requirements and background for these RF-field strength measurement tasks and their specific needs of technical equipment were discussed. Following that, we evaluate and compare up-to-date RF-measurement methods like field probes measurements or frequency selective methods using antennas. Here we consider point screening methods like the 'isotropic spatial averaging method' and the currently most popular 'sweeping method' for isotropic and frequency selective measurements as well as monitoring methods. Afterwards we focus on frequency selective, isotropic long-term EMF measurements performed with a 'field nose' system in the frequency range from 80 MHz up to 2.5 GHz and present effective methods for data reduction of such long-term measurements.

articleTitle: Intrinsically conducting nanocomposites: high performance electromagnetic shielding materials
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: The new ways of processing intrinsically conducting polymers as polyaniline (PANI) permits to conceive nano-composites with high conductivities. The blends of PANI with polyurethane showed a very low percolation threshold (<1%) and the dielectric properties can be tuned easily and precisely with the mass fraction of PANI in the blends. The performances of the materials in term of electromagnetic shielding (SE) were evaluated on a wide range of frequencies (50 MHz-100 GHz). Electromagnetic shielding effectiveness from 30 to 90 dB were found for mono or multi layer samples in the X and Ku band. From the measured physical properties (conductivity, permittivity) of the materials used as a data base, the genetic algorithm permits to optimize the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness to obtain very lightweight materials with a thickness below one millimeter with a SE superior to 40 dB in the 50 MHz-100 GHz band. By optimizing the materials for a desired value of shielding effectiveness, the quantity of PANI in the blends is reduced and then their mechanical properties are nearly those of the polyurethane. An other important advantage for industrial applications is a reduction of the cost of production of the materials.

articleTitle: Russian register of shiping EMC requirements for electrical and electronic equipment and systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Russian register of shipping is the main body for certification of shipboard equipment. EMC requirements of Russian register are stronger than EMC requirements of IEC (60533, 60945), IACS (E10), EN and Gosstandart for electrical and electronic equipment. Additional EMC tests for systems in ships are required.

articleTitle: Pulse voltage measurement in EMC
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: Pulse voltage measurements are used for electromagnetic environment investigation, test simulator calibration and for estimation of effectiveness of noise suppression devices. Construction of voltage dividers, connection to the circuits and grounding are discussed. Results of experiments with different dividers, grounding and electromagnetic field influence are presented.

articleTitle: Impulse testing equipment for military applications
publicationTitle: IEEE 6th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology, 2005.
abstract: MIL 461 is arguably one of the most widely used test standards for military electronics suppliers, due largely to the fact that it covers inter-service operability issues. This standard draws on the NATO (stanag) and civilian (ANSI/IEEE) experiences. In line with other international standards, the test event is now specified at the point of connection to an EUT which includes all coupling elements in the system calibration. This has the immediate effect of precluding test equipment that was designed for previous MIL 461 standards. This paper will differentiate between the current and previous editions of MIL 461, describing changes to the test requirements both in terms of equipment requirements and calibration procedures.

abstract: The following topics are dealt with: shipboard EMC; electrical power equipment; electromagnetic interaction-shielding; radiofrequency spectrum application; radiomonitoring; radio communication system; antennas; propagation; radio electronic equipment design; certification; test equipment; EM field biological effect.
